Overview

Company Overview

Portkey is building the control plane for production AI applications — the infrastructure layer that powers, observes, and manages how AI systems run in the real world.

From routing LLM requests and handling fallbacks to monitoring performance, reliability, and cost, Portkey helps fast-growing teams ship AI features with confidence.

We work with teams running mission-critical AI workloads, where uptime, observability, and performance matter. If you’re excited about AI infrastructure, developer experience, and building tools that power real-world AI products, you’ll feel at home here.

Challenge Overview

This is not a typical hackathon challenge. It’s a hands-on simulation of what it actually feels like to work on production-grade AI systems.

You’ll tackle problems that mirror real scenarios engineers face while shipping and maintaining AI infrastructure at scale. The focus is on how you think, how you debug, and how you reason about systems when things aren’t perfect.

Expect challenges around understanding system behavior, tracing failures, making smart trade-offs, and communicating decisions clearly. This is about clarity over flash, depth over demos, and ownership over shortcuts.

Strong performers won’t just walk away with prizes. They’ll stand out to the Portkey team as engineers who can operate close to real-world production systems.

Who Should Participate

This challenge is ideal for:

  • Engineers who enjoy solving real-world problems
  • Developers curious about how AI systems work in production
  • Builders who enjoy debugging and system-level thinking
  • People who value clean design, reasoning, and clarity

You do not need prior experience with Portkey to participate.

Beyond the Build

Great work deserves to be seen. Standout participants will be rewarded with exciting prizes and get the opportunity to be recognised by the Portkey team, with exceptional performers potentially turning this challenge into a full-time role.

Why Participate

  • Work on real AI infrastructure problems
  • Learn how production systems behave at scale
  • Get evaluated on thinking, not trivia
  • Build something meaningful, not just a demo
  • Interact with engineers solving real-world AI problems

If you enjoy building, debugging, and learning fast — this challenge is built for you.

Themes

Living LLM Pricing & Capability Catalog

LLM providers are constantly changing their pricing, context limits, supported features, rate limits, and even model availability. These updates are spread across documentation pages, blogs, APIs, and changelogs, and are often not clearly announced. As a result, it becomes difficult for teams to keep track of what is accurate and up to date. The goal is to build a living system that continuously tracks LLM providers and their models, maintaining a single, canonical catalog of models, pricing, limits, capabilities, and related metadata. Instead of being a static reference, this catalog updates over time as providers make changes. The system should use agents to ingest data from multiple sources such as scraping, APIs, and feeds, while maintaining state to avoid unnecessary re-crawling. It should detect semantic changes rather than simple text differences, ensuring that meaningful updates are captured. Every field in the catalog should include metadata such as its source, last verified timestamp, and a confidence score. When conflicting information is found, the system should surface it clearly instead of overwriting existing data. As extensions, the system can support pricing change alerts, historical pricing tracking, breaking-change detection, and expose the catalog as a machine-readable registry in formats like JSON.

Smart Prompt Parser & Canonicalisation Engine

AI systems tend to accumulate thousands of prompts over time. Many of these prompts are duplicated or only slightly modified, which makes them hard to reason about and nearly impossible to optimize at scale. Teams often lose visibility into which prompts are truly distinct and which are just variations of the same underlying intent. The goal is to build a smart prompt parser and canonicalisation engine that analyzes a collection of prompts and organizes them meaningfully. The system should cluster semantically equivalent prompts, extract reusable prompt templates by identifying constant parts and variable slots, and track how prompts evolve over time. This includes detecting entirely new prompt families as well as identifying new variable sets added to existing families. The system should rely on semantic similarity rather than simple string matching to ensure accurate grouping. Grouping decisions must be explainable so teams understand why prompts were clustered together. It should support incremental processing as new prompts are added, and use confidence thresholds to control when prompts are merged, ensuring accuracy and trust in the system.

Ai Machine LearningRead more

Fine-Tuned OSS Guardrail Models

Prompt-based guardrails are often expensive to run, slow in production, and inconsistent in their behavior across different inputs and edge cases. Relying purely on prompts for safety and policy enforcement does not scale well as systems grow in complexity and traffic. The goal is to fine-tune one or more open-source models to act as specialized guardrail models. Instead of general-purpose prompting, these models are trained specifically to detect and enforce safety and policy constraints with higher reliability and lower runtime cost. Teams can fine-tune these guardrail models for specific use cases such as PII detection, prompt injection detection, content moderation, policy violation detection, and unsafe instruction detection. Each model can focus on a narrow responsibility rather than trying to cover everything at once. The system should include a clear strategy for synthetic data generation, along with a well-defined training and evaluation split. Evaluation should prioritize precision to minimize false positives, especially in production scenarios. A runtime inference demo should show how the guardrail model performs in real-time workflows, and the project should include a thoughtful discussion of failure cases and limitations. The emphasis should be on depth of understanding and execution rather than covering too many use cases at once.

Ai Machine LearningRead more

Cost–Quality Optimisation via Historical Replay

Model choices in AI systems are often made blindly, without a clear understanding of how different models perform on real production workloads. Teams rarely have an easy way to compare cost, quality, and safety trade-offs using their own historical data. The goal is to build a system that replays historical prompt–completion data across different models and guardrails. By running the same inputs through multiple configurations, the system can evaluate and compare metrics such as cost, output quality, and refusal rates. Based on these evaluations, the system should recommend better trade-offs tailored to actual usage patterns. The expected output is a clear, actionable recommendation, such as showing that switching from one model to another reduces cost by a certain percentage while only marginally impacting quality.

Eligibility

All participants are eligible to register for Portkey AI Builders Challenge

Rules

1. Applicability

This Code of Conduct applies to all participants, mentors, judges, organizers, and partners involved in the Portkey Builders Challenge.

It applies across:

  • Hackathon workspaces (online & offline)
  • Mentorship sessions and evaluations
  • Communication channels (WhatsApp/Discord, email, calls)
  • Submissions, demos, and discussions

By participating, you agree to follow these guidelines throughout the event.

2. Originality & Fair Participation

We value real skills and honest problem-solving.

  • All work must be done during the hackathon period.
  • Pre-built projects or reused codebases are not allowed.
  • Open-source libraries and APIs may be used, but must be clearly disclosed.
  • Any form of plagiarism, misrepresentation, or unfair practice will lead to immediate disqualification.

3. Purpose of the Hackathon

This is a hiring-focused hackathon, designed to evaluate:

  • Problem-solving ability
  • Debugging and system thinking
  • Communication and clarity
  • Real-world engineering judgment

It is not about flashy demos, but about how you think and build.

4. Professional Conduct

All participants are expected to maintain a respectful and professional environment.

Unacceptable behavior includes:

  • Harassment, discrimination, or intimidation
  • Offensive language or personal attacks
  • Disruptive or uncooperative behavior
  • Misrepresentation of work or credentials

Portkey maintains zero tolerance for misconduct.

5. Inclusivity & Respect

We are committed to creating a safe and inclusive environment for everyone, regardless of:

  • Gender or gender identity
  • Sexual orientation
  • Race, nationality, or ethnicity
  • Educational or professional background

Everyone deserves equal opportunity and respect.

6. Data & AI Ethics

If your solution involves AI or data:

  • Do not use sensitive or private data
  • Avoid generating harmful or misleading outputs
  • Ensure responsible use of LLMs and APIs
  • Respect user privacy and ethical AI practices

Any misuse of data or unsafe AI behavior may lead to disqualification.

7. Submissions & Evaluation

  • Submissions must be completed before the deadline.

  • Late or incomplete submissions may not be considered.

  • Projects will be evaluated based on:

    • Problem understanding
    • Technical execution
    • Clarity of approach
    • Debugging & reasoning
    • Role fit

Judges’ decisions will be final.

8. Communication & Availability

  • Participants must be reachable during the hackathon window.

  • Shortlisted candidates may be contacted for:

    • Clarifications
    • Interviews
    • Further technical discussions

  • Clear and respectful communication is expected at all times.

9. Hiring Disclaimer

  • Participation does not guarantee employment.
  • This hackathon is part of Portkey’s hiring process.
  • Selected participants may be fast-tracked to interviews or offers.
  • Final hiring decisions rest solely with Portkey.
  • The salary/package will be according to the industry standards.

10. Intellectual Property

  • Participants retain ownership of their work.
  • Portkey may review submissions strictly for evaluation and hiring purposes.
  • Any future use of submissions will require explicit permission.

11. Rule Changes & Authority

  • Portkey reserves the right to update rules or timelines if required.

  • Any violation of rules may result in:

    • Disqualification
    • Removal from the event
    • Disqualification from future Portkey hiring processes

12. Final Note

This hackathon is an opportunity to:

  • Learn how real AI systems operate
  • Showcase your problem-solving skills
  • Work on real-world engineering challenges
  • Get noticed by a high-impact AI infrastructure company

Come curious. Build honestly. Think deeply.
